# Actual pinned Qwen inference

The unchanged Mluva v1.6.0 client at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f` was run against real pinned `b11011` CPU and Vulkan binaries and Qwen3-ASR 1.7B Q4_0 weights with the Q8_0 audio projector. All nine imported source/resource files were checked against that commit before collecting results. The native comparison invokes the public Rust client through its existing development driver; the actual llama runtime performs inference. No synthetic runtime responses are used in this check.

`released-qwen-inference.json` SHA-256: `99cec4ce6c21f2681a0d680b8fb22a366ad5c3e3d5b93194d799e6d55f50237c`. It records two device sessions with fourteen actions: ten successful recognitions, two explicit closes and two cancellations during actual provisional output. All 362 provisional callback hashes/character counts and every final transcript/metadata observation match the native client. Hashes protect the exact comparison without publishing the sample transcripts. Four actual model processes match arguments, cleared environment, null standard streams and private key/directory modes; their disappearance and key deletion are checked independently through `/proc` after the driver returns.

Input is the [public English and Chinese audio used by Qwen's own examples](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/README.md). Original lengths/checksums and normalized PCM lengths/checksums are frozen in the fixture. The English input is 48 kHz/24-bit and is normalized to 16 kHz signed little-endian PCM16; the Chinese input already has the required format. Tests use FFmpeg to normalize public fixture audio and the native WAV encoder to form recognition inputs. This is test-input preparation, not a production Python helper or an audio-device capture. Repeating the English clip produces 30.1025 seconds and exercises the real 25-second block split, joined final text and accumulated provisional text.

Both devices cover automatic and forced English/Chinese recognition, retained weights across requests, explicit unload/restart and permanent cancellation after the first actual transcript callback. This machine's pinned Vulkan runtime enumerates the NVIDIA GPU as `Vulkan1`; the client correctly selects it instead of the first available Vulkan device. CPU and GPU have different frozen results for the multiple-block clip; the native client matches the release separately on each device. This is same-machine/component acceptance, not a general accuracy evaluation or a promise of identical decoder output across CPU/GPU hardware.

The ignored test was explicitly executed successfully with Rust 1.95. It downloads both pinned runtime archives through the production native installer into disposable storage. An explicit `MLUVA_QWEN_WEIGHTS` path may supply public weights to avoid a repeated 1.6 GB download; each file is verified against the pinned size and SHA before copying into the owned test store. Without that optional test setting, the native installer downloads and verifies the weights itself. No installed model/runtime/cache is used for inference or modified. Shader caches and temporary credentials are private to the disposable roots. No microphone, provider account, user content, host input or visible desktop interaction is used.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test qwen \
  inference::actual_pinned_qwen_cpu_and_gpu_match_released_recognition \
  -- --ignored --exact --nocapture
```

The check requires Linux `/proc`, FFmpeg, network access to pinned public assets and a compatible physical NVIDIA Vulkan device. Its frozen physical results were collected on the same i7-12700H/RTX A1000 laptop used by the existing model verification; other hardware/driver acceptance requires corresponding independent reference observations. This check observes ordinary close and active-inference cancellation; interruption during model loading, full startup/stream deadlines, actual 5 GB RSS overflow and abrupt application crash remain required. Broader language/quality coverage, provider/controller integration, paced Live capture, full UI workflows, native Whisper/Parakeet, distribution, Python removal and whole-app performance remain pending.

Private logs contain component durations from one release run (CPU/GPU 26.993/18.966 seconds) and two native runs (CPU 24.982–27.364 seconds; GPU 17.227–17.285 seconds). The runs are sequential, model pages may already be cached and each uses its own shader cache. These observations are not a controlled performance distribution or evidence of whole-app improvement. The ordinary workspace still passes 104 tests; this check is the sixth context-dependent ignored test, executed separately. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Installed app/widget remain v1.6.0.
